served.stem: One student can enter a stack of survey forms in 5 hours and another can enter the same stack in 4 hours. Working together, how many hours does the stack take?

answer.line: Rates add: 1/5 + 1/4 = 9/20 of the stack per hour, so the whole stack takes 20/9, about 2.22 hours.

steps: Turn each time into a rate. Picture a stack of 20 forms: one student enters 4 an hour, the other 5.
Rates add, times do not. Together they enter 4 + 5 = 9 forms an hour.
Two hours clear 18 forms, and the last 2 take 2/9 of an hour. Total: 20/9, about 2.22 hours.
Check it: together has to beat the faster student alone, 4 hours. 2.22 does.

choices.note: 0.45 is the combined rate, 9/20 of the stack per hour. Flip it to get the hours: 20/9.
4 hours is the faster student working alone. A helper has to shorten the job.
4.5 averages the two times. Two people working together finish faster than either one alone.
5 + 4 = 9 adds the times, as if each entered a whole stack in turn. Rates add; times do not.

student.lockIt: Working together: add the rates, then flip. Together always beats the faster worker alone.
